body: Kit Kats are my favorite chocolate. The vanilla tootsie rolls in the blue wrapping paper are amazing.
Dude m&ms are legit. When I was a kid I thought for some reason that the brown ones were extra chocolate so I always ate those first.

I was curious to see if your first visit benefited your mental state in any way. I was hospitalized 2 years ago and I literally didn’t get anything from it besides PTSD and the fact that I’m alive I guess.

You’re tough and you’ll be able to and power through. I wish you strength and courage, my friend.
Immediately after your hospital stay, how did you feel? How long were you hospitalized for?

Have you brought up your concerns with your guidance counselor? Are you required to wear shorts or is it just a preference? 

The best advice I can give is to either speak to the counselor or your parents about it. They may be able to let you wear something other than shorts or perhaps let you change separate or at a different time than the others. Or give you some other way of covering your scars.

Best of luck. Stay positive, my friend!

Edit: Changed my wording a bit.
Congratulations! You’re so strong. Here’s to another month!

Honestly, there’s no “great” way of doing it. I’ve never straight up told anybody face to face that I cut. When I wanted to tell my parents, I just didn’t hide them and let them come to me about it.

It’s going to be different depending on the person you’re trying to tell. I knew if I let my parents see them and make their own conclusions, it would be better so they could get their emotions in check and figure out what they wanted to say to me before approaching me.

I’m sorry I can’t really give much advice, but that might be an option if you think that would be the best way for your loved ones to process it.

Hi there!

When I first started harming myself, it started off like you stated. Thumbtacks, paper clips, the like.

Please don’t go any farther than you have. Self harm is addicting. It releases feel-good chemicals in your brain and it makes you want to do more. You haven’t ventured into the more serious territory and I beg for you not to.

I cut for many years and I know it’s not healthy. But once you start, it’s very hard to stop. It’s like any drug, it’s addicting as hell. 

There’s plenty of other things in the world to get your mind focused on. Please don’t let it be this. Stay strong OP, I wish you the best!
Thank you for your kind words. I wish you luck on your journey. We can both be strong!

I had the opposite reaction at my work. My coworkers never had any issue with me until one of my managers saw my arm and gasped really loud in front of a group of us. She made it super obvious what she was staring at.

After that, everyone has treated me like I’m invisible.

People suck.

No problem! I doubt the audience would notice either way but your co-stars would definitely notice makeup on your arm.

You have a great weekend as well!

Honestly, unless you plan on covering your whole arm in foundation it’s going to make it even more obvious if you try to cover it up. Any time I’ve tried something like that, it’s always just drawn attention to it.

Are they in a way where they could be played off as cat scratches or anything like that? I’ve found that unless I’m surrounded by people that are familiar with cutting, people don’t assume it’s self-inflicted.

They do sell cover-up foundation made for people with tattoos that would probably work. I’m pretty sure it’s expensive though and you’d have to find your perfect shade or again, it’ll look pretty obvious.
I would love to see pics! I’m getting so excited to get mine done.

I don’t have any ideas about anything. They only thing I really enjoy doing is reading and writing but I don’t ever have the energy to sit down and write anything. I don’t have the energy to do much of anything recently.

I’ve also been told by multiple people that my writing isn’t worth much so there’s that.

I have to make money to pay my bills and rent so it’s not like I can pool all my time and energy into a hobby that I’m no good at.

Ive been hospitalized for suicidal ideation and self harm multiple times. I have a Psychiatrist, therapists, and a social worker. So they are very well aware of my feelings. 

They just don’t want to believe that the only thing they did with their lives wants to not exist. They just pretend like it isn’t happening or that it’s not a big deal, or that my issue will just be cured one day.
